title: Design it first: the review
goal: Before writing code, write the design for "an LLM inference platform" in the 7-step interview format. You will build this design over the next 10 stages, then compare it with the model answer.

concepts.how: The 7 steps structure the whole review: requirements, estimation, API, data model, high-level design, deep dives, wrap-up.
Separate functional requirements (chat, streaming, batch) from the numbers that drive the design (TTFT and TPOT targets, tenants, peak load).
Back-of-envelope: requests per second at peak, tokens per second, concurrent streams by Little's law.
The reference architecture you are designing toward: gateway, admission, router, replicas, batch tier.
Name each block (load balancer, queue, cache, vector index, rate limiter) and why it is there.
Every deep dive ends with what you gave up: hit rate vs correctness, fail-open vs fail-closed.

checkpoints.text: I wrote functional and non-functional requirements, including TTFT and TPOT targets with percentiles.
I estimated peak requests/s, output tokens/s and concurrent streams, showing the arithmetic.
I drew the high-level design with gateway, router, model replicas, cache, queue and data stores.
I picked two deep dives and wrote the trade-off I am accepting in each.
